comment: Ground truth for the taint precision probe suite (analysis-strategy.md §5.5). One family per precision axis. Lines are 1-BASED source lines of `print(...)` call statements (the lifter's loc.line is 0-based; the runner adds 1). expect: tp = real flow, must hit; clean = no flow, must NOT hit (FP guard); fp = no flow but the CURRENT rung hits (EXPECTED false positive; closes_at_rung says which ladder rung should kill it, null = structural/wontfix); fn = real flow the current rung misses (KNOWN false negative; closes_at_rung says which rung should catch it). The runner FAILS on any deviation in either direction — an expected-fp/fn that stops reproducing means the ladder moved and this file must be updated deliberately. HISTORY: annotated at rung 0 (t-P1; tp=11 fp=4 fn=4). Rung 1 (t-P2, the on-demand alias engine + points_to-fed call-graph refinement + heap-fact summary endpoints, default rung now 1) flipped: a4 fp→clean (store base refined to mkobj's alloc site, disjoint from o's), a5 fp→clean (balanced call/return hop proves p===o, strong update kills the taint), b3 fn→tp (param-callee bridged to the caller's AllocClosure body), e5 fn→tp (Object.assign alias-flow endpoint matches heap facts by positive points-to intersection). b2 evaluated honestly and RE-TAGGED rung 1→2 (environment identity, not heap aliasing — see its rationale). New table: tp=13 fp=2 fn=2. t-P3 (prototype-chain summary lookup): e6–e10 added — receiver-typed builtin calls (local alloc array, own-method shadow FP control, global-store provenance string, for-of iterator protocol, repeat-count clean guard). New table: tp=16 fp=3 fn=2. t-P4 (full gap propagator): e11–e16 added — the Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter gap trio (gap enter/return channels, param-callee resolution through the may-direction arm, the unresolved-callback honest fallback); e13 is an EXPECTED fp (unknown-base may-alias on the VM-allocated map result, closes at rung 2; the gap return channel itself is pinned silent by the mechanism twin). New table: tp=20 fp=4 fn=2.

es2abc.why: Newest pinned image version (precision axes are version-independent; the suite is not a version matrix). Baseline profile = --opt-level=0, the least-transformed bytecode, and it still carries the line-number table (verified: lifted Inst.loc present, 0-based). Script mode matches the corpus' local-fixture compiles.

config_notes: builtin_summaries on, seed_all_functions on, native_identity on — all defaults. Every probe declares `var TAINT = "tainted"` at top level (script mode → global record) so the VM run is clean AND every read compiles to TryGetGlobal("TAINT"), which is the source.

probes.rationale: Same alloc site, store then load of one field — the rung-0 baseline heap case (site-keyed facts meet at the key).
Distinct alloc sites, same field name — rung-0 site keying must keep them apart (disjoint non-empty site sets ⇒ no alias).
Store through a Mov alias — the def-chain walk resolves p to o's site, so the store/load keys meet.

Store through a call-result (unknown) base keyed the fact with an EMPTY site set at rung 0, may-aliasing every load of the field (the FP this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED clean at rung 1 (t-P2): the engine's memoized backward points_to hops the call into mkobj and keys the store with mkobj's alloc site — disjoint from o's site, so the hit dies.

Sanitizing store through an unproven alias (call result) was a WEAK update at rung 0 — the taint survived even though p === o at runtime (the FP this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED clean at rung 1 (t-P2): the balanced call/return hop resolves p's points_to to o's single alloc site (id returns its formal; the context stack binds it to THIS call's argument), so the update is strong and kills the taint.

Phi of the aliased object and a fresh one — the site union still intersects o's site (weak update path exercised). Runtime never takes the fresh-object branch (TAINT.length is 7), so the flow is real.
Captured variable promoted to a lexical-env slot by es2abc; the LexVar fact is a state base and crosses the resolved direct call edge into the closure body.

LexVar keys are function-agnostic (level, slot) pairs — innocent's slot-(0,0) capture merges with main's tainted slot-(0,0) capture across resolved call edges. EVALUATED HONESTLY at rung 1 (t-P2): this is an ENVIRONMENT-identity problem, not a heap-alias problem — PutLexVar/GetLexVar carry no environment operand in the IR, so separating the two environments requires keying facts by lexenv-object identity (NewLexEnv sites + the closure-capture linkage), which is a heap-model extension belonging to the rung-2 whole-program PTA, not to rung 1's demand-driven value points_to. RE-TAGGED closes_at_rung 1→2 rather than fake-fixed. The FP still reproduces at rung 1.

The callback is invoked through a PARAMETER callee (register's cb) — unresolved at rung 0, so no call edge carried the captured taint into cb's body (the FN this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED tp at rung 1 (t-P2): CallGraph::refine_with_points_to asks the engine for the callee value's sites; the unbalanced caller fan-out traces register's cb param to main's AllocClosure site, the bridge maps it to cb's DefineFunc body, and the solver steps in (§5.4's one engine, two consumers).

Phi of two closures — set-valued resolution steps into BOTH; the real flow through id is found. The konst over-approximation is invisible at sink granularity because the runtime path really goes through id (TAINT.length is 7 > 0). (The N66 frame-slot binding fix — args[i] -> params[3+i] under the vendored 0xF callType default — landed in problem.rs call_flow; this probe was the red-first evidence and flipped to TP when the fix landed.)

A USER-DEFINED top-level `print` takes over the global binding; name-keyed sink matching keys on TryGetGlobal("print"), so the sink fires on a call whose binding is user code. The corpus' own reality (its call-site head is user globals named foo/f/testXxx): name keying cannot tell a redefined global from the host builtin. No rung closes this; recorded as dispatch-axis FP evidence for the rung-1->2 trigger discussion. (A LOCAL `function print` shadow cannot exercise the axis: es2abc mangles local function names to `#*@0*#print`, which never matches.)

Method-valued callee off a local object: dispatch unresolved at rung 0 (no receiver typing), the identity heuristic carries arg taint to the call result. TP via the fallback ladder, not via dispatch — documents what currently saves unresolved method calls.

Callee loaded from an array element: dispatch unresolved, no call edge enters the stored closure, the sink inside never sees the taint. §5.5's APAK axis — the rung-2 call-graph layer (callee resolution through element points-to) closes it.
throw→handler is the ONLY route from source to sink — intraprocedural exception dispatch (T5).
The thrown value is clean; a tainted local stays live across the try but is never thrown nor printed. Two clean sinks (catch binding, normal path) — FP guards.

Taint thrown inside a RESOLVED callee lands on the caller's catch binding — return_flow Throw wiring (T5/T10). (The N66 frame-slot binding fix — args[i] -> params[3+i] under the vendored 0xF callType default — landed in problem.rs call_flow; this probe was the red-first evidence and flipped to TP when the fix landed.)

The thrower is a top-level function — a global binding, so the call edge is unresolved at rung 0 (the corpus' ~97% unknown-callee reality) and the tainted argument never enters boom. The rung-2 call-graph layer's global-call resolution closes it.
Exclusive summary application: JSON.stringify's param(0)→return flow carries the taint. The counter assertion proves the SUMMARY fired (not the identity heuristic).

Exclusive pure-test summary: Object.is's result is a fresh boolean, operand taint killed on the call-to-return edge. Proves summary application beats the native identity heuristic (which would otherwise taint the result).

No summary, resolved callee with a body — the solver steps INTO the body. The counter assertion proves body_step (the flow does not ride the identity heuristic). (The N66 frame-slot binding fix — args[i] -> params[3+i] under the vendored 0xF callType default — landed in problem.rs call_flow; this probe was the red-first evidence and flipped to TP when the fix landed.)
No summary, external-but-named callee — conservative keep + identity heuristic (fallback ladder rung 3). The named-miss assertion proves NO summary fired for parseInt.

Object.assign's alias_flow matched WHOLE-VALUE taint on param(1) only — the source literal's FIELD taint is heap-keyed and never entered the target (the FN this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED tp (t-P2): summary flow endpoints now match heap facts whose site set positively intersects the endpoint value's site resolution. The match is NOT oracle-gated — it fires whenever site resolution knows the argument's sites (the rung-0 local walk suffices for this locally-allocated literal; the rung-1 engine matters when the argument needs the interprocedural query). A/B evidence: e5 flips at BOTH oracle rungs; a4/a5/b3 flip only at rung 1.

t-P3 prototype-resolution path: a local AllocArray receiver types Array.prototype; push's alias flow tags the [AnyIndex] element channel and pop's Field([AnyIndex])→Return flow carries it to the popped value. TP.

t-P3 own-method shadow collision: an array with its OWN pop still types Array.prototype (the shadow store is invisible at the method load — store-to-load of function values is opaque), so the BUILTIN pop summary fires on a call that runs user code. EXPECTED FP, the c2 lesson: family-keyed collision is structural; closes at rung 2 (whole-program PTA resolving property stores into loads). The shadow precedes the push so the registered AnyIndex-wildcard strong-kill does not remove the element taint first. Ground truth: own pop returns 7 — clean.

t-P3 global-store provenance: the receiver is a local alias of the TAINT global; points-to is opaque through global loads, but the module's stores of TAINT (a string literal) type the receiver String.prototype through the flow-insensitive global-record scan; charCodeAt's Base→Return flow carries the content taint. TP.

t-P3 for-of protocol: getiterator over an AllocArray types Iterator.prototype; the array's [AnyIndex] element taint re-keys onto the iterator at the GetIterator flow rule and rides Iterator.prototype.next's Field([AnyIndex])→Return flow into the {value,done} wrapper; the .value read picks it up. TP.

t-P3 repeat-count FP guard: the constant receiver types String.prototype; repeat's summary flows Base→Return only, so the TAINTED COUNT goes nowhere — pins summary application beating the native-identity heuristic (which would taint the result), e2's prototype-path analogue. Ground truth: "x".repeat("tainted") is "" — clean.

t-P4 full gap propagator: forEach's callback resolves to a local closure; the array's [AnyIndex] element taint enters the callback's formal 0 through the gap enter rules and the print inside the body fires. TP.
t-P4 gap return channel: map's callback returns its tainted formal; the gap return wires it onto the result array's [AnyIndex] elements and the indexed read fires. TP.

t-P4 negative control: map's callback ignores its parameter and returns a constant — the result elements carry no REAL taint (result taint comes from the callback RETURN, not the base; the mechanism-level isolation is tests/mechanisms.rs::gap_map_callback_ignoring_param_no_return_flow). EXPECTED FP here: the map result is VM-allocated (no keyed site), so the indexed load through it meets the SOURCE array's Heap(site).[AnyIndex] fact via the load rule's unknown-base may-alias wildcard (either side unknown ⇒ may reach). Closes when summary results get call-site-keyed allocations.
t-P4: filter's predicate return taints nothing (return channel None); the result's elements are the base's kept elements via the static Field([AnyIndex])→ReturnField([AnyIndex]) flow. TP.

t-P4 honest fallback: the callback is an opaque global load — no gap edge, the element taint never enters user code (mini-gap tag only; gap_sites_unresolved records the site). forEach's result is undefined. Clean.

t-P4 points-to arm: the callback reaches the gap site through a resolved local helper's parameter — the rung-1 engine's caller fan-out resolves it to the caller's closure alloc, and the receiver param types Array through the same engine. TP.
